comment:purpose: A second domain onboarded as data alone: `hu-tax`, a Hungarian tax vault, with no TypeScript edit anywhere. The PROFILE ships; the CORPUS does not — the documents it labels are the owner's and are not in this repository.
comment:mount-point: `repoRoot` names a MOUNT POINT, not a directory this repo contains: the owner puts — or symlinks — their Hungarian vault at `dp-gnosis/corpora/hu-tax`, and the three `corpusRoots` (analizis, leiras, melo) are read underneath it. `--repo-root` outranks this key (flag > profile > default), so the same profile reads a vault mounted anywhere else without being edited. With NOTHING mounted, `ingest` REFUSES: it names the first corpus root that matched no markdown files and the mount point it looked under, and the process exits NON-ZERO before writing anything — so the profile cannot half-ingest into a wrong corpus. That is a REFUSED INGEST, and it is a different fact from BOTH an empty corpus and the `index-empty` exit 3, which reports an INDEX holding nothing over a NON-EMPTY atoms directory — the three must not be read as the same failure.
comment:locations: This profile owns BOTH its `atomsDir` and its `indexPath` for the same two reasons the web-research profile does. The index default is per-ADAPTER, not per-profile, so two instances left on the default write the same index file and the later run overwrites the earlier one in silence. A shared atoms directory is worse than overwriting: `ingest` makes the tree hold EXACTLY the current run's write set, so whichever profile ingests last PRUNES the other's atoms. The `.dp-gnosis-owner` marker refuses a directory stamped by another profile, so the collision is caught rather than suffered — but the refusal is an error to avoid, and setting these two keys is how it is avoided.
comment:types: knowledge, teaching, vendor-doc and meta are all names the SHIPPED type vocabulary already carries. Types are CLOSED while domains are open: `asType` falls back to the shipped `DEFAULT_ATOM_TYPE` for an unknown name and `--type` validates against the shipped `ATOM_TYPES`, so a profile-only type would be silently relabelled at read time and unusable as a filter. A new type must be added to the shipped vocabulary; this profile therefore invents none.
comment:rules: `analizis` and `leiras` carry a type each — analysis is knowledge, descriptions are teaching — while `melo` (work material) is claimed for the domain only and falls to `defaultType` knowledge.

comment:locations: CORRECTED 2026-08-22 (R4.1). `repoRoot` named `dp-gnosis/corpora/hu-tax`, a tree that has never existed on this machine; the documents are mounted at `dp-gnosis/corpus-hu` and carry the exact three `corpusRoots` this profile already declared (analizis 17 / leiras 4 / melo 55 .md). That single wrong path is the whole of what blocked DoD #4. `atomsDir` and `indexPath` moved under a hu-tax-OWNED parent (`dp-gnosis/cache/hu-tax/`) for the reason GNOSIS-GUIDE.md § Landmines states: `writeManifest` writes `corpus-manifest.json` to `dirname(atomsDir)`, so ingesting into `dp-gnosis/cache/` directly would have OVERWRITTEN the manifest that `web-research` (319 atoms) owns there. The old empty `dp-gnosis/cache/index/atoms-hu-tax-fts5.db` (16 § 4 D11) is superseded by this move and may be deleted.
comment:defaultPrf: Owner-approved 2026-08-21: RM3 pseudo-relevance feedback is a SERVED default on this profile, at the MEASURED frozen cell fbDocs 10 / fbTerms 40 / alpha 0.5 — the cell `SERVED_PRF_PARAMS` (src/prf.ts) OWNS, and the one the gate was run on (qwen3-reranker-4b: vault-hu nDCG@10 +0.0323 p=0.0186; vault +0.0080 p=0.4567, not significant and adopted deliberately). It is NOT `DEFAULT_PRF_PARAMS`, whose fbTerms is 20 and which no recorded arm used. Like `defaultExcludedTypes` it is a RETRIEVE-TIME default on the CLI path alone: nothing in ingest, the port or an adapter reads it, so the bench still measures the unexpanded first pass and every recorded number stands. `--no-prf` turns it off, and the `--prf-*` flags override one member each.
